blocks.text: You can use operators like `+`, `-`, `*`, `==`, `<` with your own types. In Greengold operators map to **specific method names**: `+` → `add`, `-` → `sub`, `*` → `mul`, `/` → `div`, `%` → `rem`, `-x` → `neg`, `==` → `eq`, `<` → `lt`. `!=`, `>`, `<=`, `>=` are derived from them automatically.

blocks.prompt: Give the `Money` struct (`cents: i32`) `add` and `lt` methods. Print the sum `Money{ cents: 250 } + Money{ cents: 175 }` and whether the first `Money` is less than the second.
blocks.hint: Write `fn add(self, o: Money) -> Money` and `fn lt(self, o: Money) -> bool` in `impl Money:`.

blocks.q: Which method do you define for `a - b`?
blocks.why: The `-` operator maps to the `sub` method.
